newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz wants more repair-friendly cars.
newsitem.headline: Allianz wants more repair-friendly cars.

text.p: The level of damages paid out as a result of car accidents could be considerably lowered if cars were made more repair-friendly, Germany's insurance giant Allianz said on Wednesday.
Costs could be also be reduced with more suitable spare parts and higher tool quality, Allianz representatives said at the 25th anniversary of the Allianz technology centre (AZT).
At least 100 million marks could be saved every year if damaged plastic car parts were repaired instead of being replaced and at least 2,000 tonnes of plastic waste could be avoided, Allianz said.
Intelligent repair work on vehicle wiring would also offer savings opportunities. In one relatively sophisticated car around 2,000 metres of wire is used.
Managing director Dieter Anselm said the most recent great sucess of the AZT had been an anti-theft device, which has led to a noticable reduction in the otherwise explosive growth of car theft.
Allianz said AZT had been the only such institution to save the German insurance sector millions of marks in the last few years along with helping keep customer premiums down.
